ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: on the left side of the figure there are directions marked, upward is N, downward is S; the legend shows that the black shadow represents the noon shadow length on June 22, and the white shadow represents the noon shadow length on December 22. At city a, the black shadow on June 22 is shorter, and the white shadow on December 22 is longer; at city b, the black shadow on June 22 is longer, and the white shadow on December 22 is shorter. Then reason: the greater the noon solar altitude, the shorter the shadow of a flagpole of equal height. City a has a short shadow on the summer solstice and a long shadow on the winter solstice, indicating that city a is closer to the area of the Tropic of Cancer; city b has a short shadow on the winter solstice and a long shadow on the summer solstice, indicating that city b is closer to the area of the Tropic of Capricorn. If cities a and b are located on the same continent, then this continent should straddle the equator and extend to near the Tropics of Capricorn and Cancer. The continent that conforms to this latitude-span characteristic is the African continent.
